/-!
# Conjecture 9.76

by V. P. Shunkov

We define a *Golod group* to be the $r$-generated, $r \geq 2$, subgroup
$\langle 1 + x_1 + I, 1 + x_2 + I, \ldots, 1 + x_r + I \rangle$ of the adjoint group $1 + F/I$
of the factor-algebra $F/I$, where $F$ is a free algebra of polynomials without constant terms
in non-commuting variables $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_r$ over a field of characteristic $p > 0$,
and $I$ is an ideal of $F$ such that $F/I$ is a non-nilpotent nil-algebra (see E. S. Golod,
*Amer. Math. Soc. Transl. (2)*, **48** (1965), 103–106). Prove that in Golod groups the
centralizer of every element is infinite.

Note that Golod groups with infinite centre were constructed by A. V. Timofeenko
(*Math. Notes*, **39**, no. 5 (1986), 353–355); independently by other methods the same result
was obtained in the 90s by L. Hammoudi.

## Formalisation notes

The free algebra $F$ of polynomials without constant term is realised as the ideal of the free
(unital) associative algebra $A = k\langle x_1, \ldots, x_r\rangle$ (`FreeAlgebra k (Fin r)`)
consisting of the elements with zero constant term. Since $A = k \cdot 1 \oplus F$, an ideal of
the non-unital algebra $F$ is the same thing as a two-sided ideal $I$ of $A$ contained in $F$,
and the factor-algebra $F/I$ is the image of $F$ in $A/I$. When $F/I$ is nil, the adjoint group
$1 + F/I$ is a subgroup of the unit group $(A/I)^\times$, so the Golod group is the subgroup of
$(A/I)^\times$ generated by the elements $1 + x_i + I$.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- E. S. Golod, *On nil-algebras and finitely approximable p-groups*,
  Amer. Math. Soc. Transl. (2) **48** (1965), 103–106.
-/

justification.closest_existing_considered: FreeAlgebra.algebraMapInv (same map, but an internal auxiliary name), Ideal.span (Set.range (FreeAlgebra.ι k)) (equal ideal), MonoidAlgebra k (FreeSemigroup (Fin r)) (non-unital but lacks quotient/nilpotency API), FreeNonUnitalNonAssocAlgebra (non-associative).

justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no free non-unital associative algebra (only FreeNonUnitalNonAssocAlgebra and the unital FreeAlgebra); the algebra F of non-commutative polynomials without constant term is realised as the kernel of the constant-term homomorphism FreeAlgebra.lift k 0 on FreeAlgebra k (Fin r).

noncomputable def quotientAlgebra : Ideal (FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) :=

justification.closest_existing_considered: Ideal.map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I) F used directly inline; TwoSidedIdeal.map / RingCon.Quotient (no ideal power API); Unitization / PreQuasiregular (adjoint group of a non-unital ring, too indirect).
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.76».quotientAlgebra
justification.why_needed: The factor-algebra F/I as a concrete object: the image of the augmentation ideal in FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I, so that nil and non-nilpotent conditions can be stated with Mathlib's IsNilpotent on elements and on ideals.

blocks.docstring:

justification.closest_existing_considered: (PreQuasiregular R)ˣ from Mathlib.Algebra.Algebra.Spectrum.Quasispectrum (adjoint group of a non-unital semiring) — would require F/I as a standalone non-unital ring type; Subgroup.closure in Units is equivalent since 1 + F/I ≤ (k⟨x⟩/I)ˣ.
justification.name: Kourovka.«9.76».golodGroup
justification.why_needed: The Golod group ⟨1 + x_1 + I, …, 1 + x_r + I⟩ as a subgroup of the unit group of k⟨x⟩/I; no Mathlib notion of the adjoint group of an ideal exists in a usable form.

blocks.name: golodGroup
blocks.text:
/-- The Golod group $\langle 1 + x_1 + I, \ldots, 1 + x_r + I\rangle$: the subgroup of the unit
group of $k\langle x_1, \ldots, x_r\rangle / I$ generated by the elements $1 + x_i + I$. -/
noncomputable def golodGroup : Subgroup (FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I)ˣ :=
  Subgroup.closure
    {u | ∃ i : Fin r, (u : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) = 1 + Ideal.Quotient.mk I (ι k i)}

theorem isUnit_one_add_mk_ι (hnil : ∀ x ∈ quotientAlgebra I, IsNilpotent x) (i : Fin r) :

  (hnil _ (Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ (ι_mem_augmentationIdeal k r i))).isUnit_one_add

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 16 20]
theorem sub_one_mem_quotientAlgebra_of_mem_golodGroup {u : (FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I)ˣ}
    (hu : u ∈ golodGroup I) : (u : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1 ∈ quotientAlgebra I := by
  induction hu using Subgroup.closure_induction with
  | mem u hu =>
    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hu
    rw [hi, add_sub_cancel_left]
    exact Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ (ι_mem_augmentationIdeal k r i)
  | one => simp
  | mul u v _ _ hu hv =>
    have : ((u * v : _ˣ) : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1 =
        ((u : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1) * ((v : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1) +
          ((u : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1) + ((v : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1) := by
      push_cast; noncomm_ring
    rw [this]
    exact add_mem (add_mem (Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ hv) hu) hv
  | inv u _ hu =>
    have : ((u⁻¹ : _ˣ) : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1 =
        -(((u⁻¹ : _ˣ) : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) *
          ((u : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1)) := by
      rw [mul_sub, mul_one, Units.inv_mul, neg_sub]
    rw [this]
    exact neg_mem (Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ hu)

@[category research open, AMS 16 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.76» (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p) (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (hI : I ≤ augmentationIdeal k r)
    (hnil : ∀ x ∈ quotientAlgebra I, IsNilpotent x)
    (hnn : ¬ IsNilpotent (quotientAlgebra I))
    (g : golodGroup I) : Infinite (Subgroup.centralizer ({g} : Set (golodGroup I))) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$, let $r \geq 2$, let
$F$ be the free algebra of polynomials without constant term in the non-commuting variables
$x_1, \ldots, x_r$ over $k$, and let $I$ be an ideal of $F$ such that $F/I$ is a non-nilpotent
nil-algebra. Let $G = \langle 1 + x_1 + I, \ldots, 1 + x_r + I\rangle$ be the corresponding
Golod group. Then the centralizer in $G$ of every element $g \in G$ is infinite.

Here $F/I$ being a nil-algebra means that every element of $F/I$ is nilpotent, and $F/I$
being nilpotent would mean that $(F/I)^n = 0$ for some $n$, i.e. that all products of $n$
elements of $F/I$ vanish. Since $I \subseteq F$, the ring $k\langle x_1, \ldots, x_r\rangle / I$
is nontrivial, so the exponent $n = 0$ never witnesses nilpotence.
blocks.name: kourovka.«9.76»

/--
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$, let $r \geq 2$, let
$F$ be the free algebra of polynomials without constant term in the non-commuting variables

Golod group. Then the centralizer in $G$ of every element $g \in G$ is infinite.

Here $F/I$ being a nil-algebra means that every element of $F/I$ is nilpotent, and $F/I$

@[category research open, AMS 16 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.76» (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p) (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (hI : I ≤ augmentationIdeal k r)
    (hnil : ∀ x ∈ quotientAlgebra I, IsNilpotent x)
    (hnn : ¬ IsNilpotent (quotientAlgebra I))
    (g : golodGroup I) : Infinite (Subgroup.centralizer ({g} : Set (golodGroup I))) := by
  sorry

claims.decomposer_note: Stated as a claim (not a yes/no question), so it is a plain Prop universally quantified over all data in the definition: every r ≥ 2, every field of characteristic p > 0, every ideal I of the free non-unital algebra F = k⟨x_1,…,x_r⟩ (no constant terms) with F/I nil but not nilpotent, the subgroup G = ⟨1+x_1+I,…,1+x_r+I⟩ of the adjoint group 1+F/I, and every g ∈ G, the centralizer C_G(g) is infinite; the trailing 'Note that Golod groups with infinite centre were constructed…' is a remark reporting a solved partial result (Timofeenko 1986, Hammoudi), not a question the statement poses, so it is not a separate sub-question.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the slot faithfully; c04 was chosen for its clean reuse of Mathlib (FreeAlgebra, two-sided Ideal + Ideal.Quotient, IsNilpotent for elements and for ideals, Units, Subgroup.closure/centralizer) with only three problem-local definitions, and for its API lemma proving that the Golod group lies in the adjoint group 1 + F/I, which justifies the main modelling choice (G computed in (A/I)ˣ). Verified: F = augmentation ideal of k⟨x_1..x_r⟩, ideals of the non-unital F are exactly two-sided ideals I ≤ F (A = k·1 ⊕ F); F/I = image of F in A/I; nil = every element nilpotent (n = 0 excluded since I ≤ F ≠ ⊤); non-nilpotent = ¬ IsNilpotent (F/I) as an ideal of A/I, where J^0 = span{1} = ⊤ ≠ ⊥ and J^(n+1) = J^n * J is the span of (n+1)-fold products (checked Submodule.instPowNat / pointwiseZero); centralizer is Subgroup.centralizer {g} in the subgroup type itself (checked with pp.explicit). Edits: theorem now uses section variables k, r, I (no shadowing), added one_notMem_augmentationIdeal and unit_one_add_mk_ι_mem_golodGroup test lemmas, expanded docstrings. Builds with lake --wfail.

/-!
# Conjecture 9.76

by V. P. Shunkov

We define a *Golod group* to be the $r$-generated, $r \geq 2$, subgroup
$\langle 1 + x_1 + I, 1 + x_2 + I, \ldots, 1 + x_r + I \rangle$ of the adjoint group $1 + F/I$
of the factor-algebra $F/I$, where $F$ is a free algebra of polynomials without constant terms
in non-commuting variables $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_r$ over a field of characteristic $p > 0$,

*Amer. Math. Soc. Transl. (2)*, **48** (1965), 103–106). Prove that in Golod groups the
centralizer of every element is infinite.

Note that Golod groups with infinite centre were constructed by A. V. Timofeenko
(*Math. Notes*, **39**, no. 5 (1986), 353–355); independently by other methods the same result
was obtained in the 90s by L. Hammoudi.

## Formalisation notes

The free algebra $F$ of polynomials without constant term is realised as the ideal of the free
(unital) associative algebra $A = k\langle x_1, \ldots, x_r\rangle$ (`FreeAlgebra k (Fin r)`)

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- E. S. Golod, *On nil-algebras and finitely approximable p-groups*,
  Amer. Math. Soc. Transl. (2) **48** (1965), 103–106.
-/

open FreeAlgebra

namespace Kourovka.«9.76»

variable (k : Type*) [Field k] (r : ℕ)

/-- The free algebra $F$ of polynomials without constant term in the non-commuting variables
$x_1, \ldots, x_r$ over $k$, realised as the ideal of the free associative algebra
$k\langle x_1, \ldots, x_r\rangle$ consisting of the elements whose constant term (the value of
the algebra homomorphism sending every variable to $0$) vanishes. -/
noncomputable def augmentationIdeal : Ideal (FreeAlgebra k (Fin r)) :=
  RingHom.ker (FreeAlgebra.lift k (0 : Fin r → k) : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) →ₐ[k] k)

/-- The variables $x_i$ have no constant term, so they lie in $F$. -/
@[category API, AMS 16]
theorem ι_mem_augmentationIdeal (i : Fin r) : ι k i ∈ augmentationIdeal k r := by
  simp [augmentationIdeal, RingHom.mem_ker]

/-- The identity has constant term $1$, so it does not lie in $F$. In particular every ideal
$I \subseteq F$ is proper, and $k\langle x_1, \ldots, x_r\rangle / I$ is nontrivial. -/
@[category API, AMS 16]
theorem one_notMem_augmentationIdeal : (1 : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r)) ∉ augmentationIdeal k r := by
  simp [augmentationIdeal, RingHom.mem_ker]

variable {k r} (I : Ideal (FreeAlgebra k (Fin r))) [I.IsTwoSided]

/-- The factor-algebra $F/I$: the image of $F$ in $k\langle x_1, \ldots, x_r\rangle / I$. -/
noncomputable def quotientAlgebra : Ideal (FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) :=
  (augmentationIdeal k r).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)

/-- The Golod group $\langle 1 + x_1 + I, \ldots, 1 + x_r + I\rangle$: the subgroup of the unit
group of $k\langle x_1, \ldots, x_r\rangle / I$ generated by the elements $1 + x_i + I$. -/
noncomputable def golodGroup : Subgroup (FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I)ˣ :=
  Subgroup.closure
    {u | ∃ i : Fin r, (u : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) = 1 + Ideal.Quotient.mk I (ι k i)}

/-- When $F/I$ is nil, the generators $1 + x_i + I$ of a Golod group are units of
$k\langle x_1, \ldots, x_r\rangle / I$. -/
@[category API, AMS 16]
theorem isUnit_one_add_mk_ι (hnil : ∀ x ∈ quotientAlgebra I, IsNilpotent x) (i : Fin r) :
    IsUnit (1 + Ideal.Quotient.mk I (ι k i)) :=
  (hnil _ (Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ (ι_mem_augmentationIdeal k r i))).isUnit_one_add

/-- When $F/I$ is nil, the unit $1 + x_i + I$ lies in the Golod group. -/
@[category API, AMS 16 20]
theorem unit_one_add_mk_ι_mem_golodGroup (hnil : ∀ x ∈ quotientAlgebra I, IsNilpotent x)
    (i : Fin r) : (isUnit_one_add_mk_ι I hnil i).unit ∈ golodGroup I :=
  Subgroup.subset_closure ⟨i, rfl⟩

/-- The Golod group is contained in the adjoint group $1 + F/I$. -/
@[category API, AMS 16 20]
theorem sub_one_mem_quotientAlgebra_of_mem_golodGroup {u : (FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I)ˣ}
    (hu : u ∈ golodGroup I) : (u : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1 ∈ quotientAlgebra I := by
  induction hu using Subgroup.closure_induction with
  | mem u hu =>
    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hu
    rw [hi, add_sub_cancel_left]
    exact Ideal.mem_map_of_mem _ (ι_mem_augmentationIdeal k r i)
  | one => simp
  | mul u v _ _ hu hv =>
    have : ((u * v : _ˣ) : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1 =
        ((u : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1) * ((v : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1) +
          ((u : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1) + ((v : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1) := by
      push_cast; noncomm_ring
    rw [this]
    exact add_mem (add_mem (Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ hv) hu) hv
  | inv u _ hu =>
    have : ((u⁻¹ : _ˣ) : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1 =
        -(((u⁻¹ : _ˣ) : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) *
          ((u : FreeAlgebra k (Fin r) ⧸ I) - 1)) := by
      rw [mul_sub, mul_one, Units.inv_mul, neg_sub]
    rw [this]
    exact neg_mem (Ideal.mul_mem_left _ _ hu)

/--
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$, let $r \geq 2$, let
$F$ be the free algebra of polynomials without constant term in the non-commuting variables
$x_1, \ldots, x_r$ over $k$, and let $I$ be an ideal of $F$ such that $F/I$ is a non-nilpotent
nil-algebra. Let $G = \langle 1 + x_1 + I, \ldots, 1 + x_r + I\rangle$ be the corresponding
Golod group. Then the centralizer in $G$ of every element $g \in G$ is infinite.

Here $F/I$ being a nil-algebra means that every element of $F/I$ is nilpotent, and $F/I$
being nilpotent would mean that $(F/I)^n = 0$ for some $n$, i.e. that all products of $n$
elements of $F/I$ vanish. Since $I \subseteq F$, the ring $k\langle x_1, \ldots, x_r\rangle / I$
is nontrivial, so the exponent $n = 0$ never witnesses nilpotence.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 16 20]
theorem kourovka.«9.76» (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p) (hr : 2 ≤ r)
    (hI : I ≤ augmentationIdeal k r)
    (hnil : ∀ x ∈ quotientAlgebra I, IsNilpotent x)
    (hnn : ¬ IsNilpotent (quotientAlgebra I))
    (g : golodGroup I) : Infinite (Subgroup.centralizer ({g} : Set (golodGroup I))) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«9.76»

items: F (free algebra of polynomials without constant terms) is realised as the augmentation ideal of the unital free algebra FreeAlgebra k (Fin r), namely RingHom.ker (FreeAlgebra.lift k 0) (the constant-term homomorphism). Ideals of the non-unital algebra F are exactly two-sided ideals I of the unital algebra with I ≤ F (since k·1 acts on I by scalars), so the theorem quantifies over `(I : Ideal (FreeAlgebra k (Fin r))) [I.IsTwoSided] (hI : I ≤ augmentationIdeal k r)`.

F/I is realised as `quotientAlgebra I := (augmentationIdeal k r).map (Ideal.Quotient.mk I)`, the image of F in k⟨x⟩/I (equal to F/I since I ≤ F). Because Mathlib `Ideal` in a noncommutative ring is a left ideal, this is a left ideal whose carrier is the image set; it is automatically two-sided (Mathlib instance for maps under surjective homs).

'F/I is a nil-algebra' is `∀ x ∈ quotientAlgebra I, IsNilpotent x`. 'F/I is non-nilpotent' is `¬ IsNilpotent (quotientAlgebra I)` using the Submodule Pow/Mul structure on `Ideal (k⟨x⟩/I)` (works in the noncommutative setting via IsScalarTower B B B); N^n for n ≥ 1 is the span of n-fold products of elements of N, so N^n = 0 ⟺ all products of n elements vanish. The n = 0 case (N^0 = ⊤) never equals ⊥ because k⟨x⟩/I is nontrivial (I ≤ F ≠ ⊤), so this matches 'nilpotent algebra' exactly.

The adjoint group 1 + F/I is a subgroup of the unit group (k⟨x⟩/I)ˣ, so the Golod group is defined as `Subgroup.closure {u : (k⟨x⟩/I)ˣ | ∃ i, (u : k⟨x⟩/I) = 1 + mk I (ι k i)}`. Under the nil hypothesis every 1 + x_i + I is a unit (API lemma `isUnit_one_add_mk_ι`), so the generating set is exactly {1 + x_1 + I, …, 1 + x_r + I}; the API lemma `sub_one_mem_quotientAlgebra_of_mem_golodGroup` verifies the Golod group lies in 1 + F/I.
Characteristic p > 0 is stated as `[CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p)` (for a field this forces p prime). r ≥ 2 is `2 ≤ r`.
The centralizer of g is taken inside the Golod group: `g : golodGroup I` and `Infinite (Subgroup.centralizer ({g} : Set (golodGroup I)))`.
Hypotheses are placed as theorem binders (not inside a ∀ after `answer(sorry)`) because the problem is stated as a claim to prove, per CONTRIBUTING.md. `k : Type*` is used for generality.

For fields where no ideal I with F/I non-nilpotent nil exists (if any), the statement is vacuous for that field, exactly as in the informal statement; Golod's construction guarantees non-vacuity (e.g. over F_p).

reviewer_notes: Single slot; the trailing Timofeenko/Hammoudi remark is a reported result, not a question, and is reproduced only in the module docstring (all candidates agreed). No candidate omitted the slot. Modelling choices a reviewer should know: (1) 'characteristic p > 0' is [CharP k p] with 0 < p (equivalent to p prime for a field; c01/c05/c06 used p.Prime, also fine). (2) The Golod group is defined as the closure in (k⟨x⟩/I)ˣ of {u | ∃ i, ↑u = 1 + x_i + I}; under the nil hypothesis each 1 + x_i + I is a unit (API lemma), so this is exactly ⟨1+x_1+I,…,1+x_r+I⟩, and it is the same group whether formed in 1 + F/I or in the full unit group (API lemma shows containment in 1 + F/I). (3) If for some field of characteristic p no ideal I with F/I nil non-nilpotent exists, the statement is vacuous for that field, exactly as the informal statement. The semigroup-algebra candidates (c01, c02, c05, c06) are also faithful but rely on more bespoke definitions (iteratedProduct, IsNilAlgebra, IsNilpotentAlgebra, adjointUnit, RingCon/TwoSidedIdeal + explicit scalar-closure) and embed tactic proofs inside let-bound statements, so they were not preferred. c03/c07/c08 are equivalent alternatives (non-nilpotence via F^(n+1) ≤ I or IsNilpotent of the mapped ideal).
statement:
We define a Golod group to be the $r$-generated, $r \geq 2$, subgroup $\left< 1 + x_1+I,\right.$ $\left. 1+x_2+I,\ldots ,1+x_r+I\right>$ of the adjoint group $1 +
F/I$ of the factor-algebra $F/I$, where $F$ is a free algebra of polynomials without constant terms in non-commuting variables $x_1,
x_2, \ldots , x_r$ over a field of characteristic $p>0$, and $I$ is an ideal of $F$ such that $F/I$ is a non-nilpotent nil-algebra (see E. S. Golod, Amer. Math. Soc. Transl. (2), 48 (1965), 103–106). Prove that in Golod groups the centralizer of every element is infinite.

Note that Golod groups with infinite centre were constructed by A. V. Timofeenko (Math. Notes, 39, no. 5 (1986), 353–355); independently by other methods the same result was obtained in the 90s by L. Hammoudi.
